title: Jewellers' Gold Savings Schemes: How They Work, Risks to Check Before Diwali
excerpt: Monthly instalments for 10 or 11 months, redeemed only for jewellery at one jeweller — how the benefit, price risk and exit terms differ by scheme.
body:
• Jeweller gold savings schemes are purchase plans, not bank deposits: you pay a fixed monthly amount for typically 10 or 11 months and redeem the total only for jewellery at that jeweller.
  • The benefit differs by scheme — a cash discount such as up to 75% of one instalment, or a waiver of wastage or making charges up to a stated cap — and it is not interest.
  • Reader check before joining: confirm whether your money tracks rupees or gold weight, when the benefit vests, and whether any cash refund exists at all, because in many plans it does not.
  • GST still applies at redemption, missed instalments can reduce the benefit, and early exit usually forfeits part or all of it.

How a jeweller gold scheme actually works

A jeweller gold savings scheme is a structured purchase plan. You enrol with one jeweller, choose a fixed monthly amount, and pay it for ten or eleven months in most plans. At maturity you buy jewellery using your total deposits plus the scheme's stated benefit, according to Rupeezy's explainer on jeweller schemes. Bhima Gold's 2026 guide describes the same mechanism: contribute a fixed amount over a set number of months and redeem the accumulated value towards gold jewellery, often with a bonus instalment or a discount on making charges.

Both explainers are explicit that these are purchase plans for jewellery buying, not investment products that pay interest.

The benefit is not one thing

Schemes that sound identical can pay out in different units. Analysing the published terms of two large schemes on 1 September 2026, OroPocket's terms comparison found Tanishq Golden Harvest pays a cash discount of 75% of one month's instalment on redemption, while GRT Golden Eleven Flexi waives wastage — no wastage up to 18%, limited to the accumulated value or gold weight. Rupeezy gives the same Tanishq figure over a 10-month plan, and lists Malabar's purchase plan at 11 months with an exemption of up to 18% on making charges within caps.

A cash discount is worth the same whatever you buy. A wastage waiver is worth a lot on a heavily worked piece and close to nothing on a plain item, OroPocket noted.

Rupees or gold weight — and who carries the price risk

Some plans track deposits in rupees to be used at the prevailing gold rate at maturity, while others convert instalments into grams each month, Rupeezy said. OroPocket found no clause in the Tanishq terms converting an instalment into gold, and quoted its clause setting the gold rate as the company's rate prevailing on the date of purchase. On that design, if gold moves over the year, that movement is the buyer's. Check the equivalent clause in any scheme you consider, because the answer differs between schemes.

OroPocket explained that schemes run 10 to 11 months because deposit rules treat an advance for goods differently when it is used within 365 days, and that money paid in is a commercial advance to a retailer, not a regulated deposit, with no deposit insurance behind it. Bhima adds that a scheme is not a guaranteed-return investment.

Risks, lock-in and exit terms

Redemption is the lock-in. Rupeezy said benefits are redeemed only against jewellery purchases and cash refunds are usually not allowed, with GRT clarifying that cash refunds are not offered and GST applies at delivery. OroPocket quoted GRT terms that a balance advance will not be refunded in cash and can only be adjusted on purchase of gold or silver coins.

Timing can also surprise buyers. OroPocket said Tanishq's discount becomes eligible after 366 days from enrolment, with redemption required before day 400, even though ten instalments finish earlier. Early exit reduces the benefit on published ladders in the schemes it reviewed, and missed payments can reduce the discount. Bhima's guide likewise warns that missing instalments can affect the benefit, early-exit terms vary, and full benefits may not apply on early redemption. GST is charged at billing on gold value and making charges, Rupeezy noted — budget for it at purchase.

What to check before the first instalment

For a diaspora reader saving in India for a wedding or Diwali purchase, the question is not which scheme advertises the largest percentage, but whether you are certain you will buy from that jeweller within its redemption window. If not, the purchase-plan structure is the wrong shape.

Use the checklist card with this article before enrolling, keep every receipt and enrolment document, as Rupeezy advises, and verify final terms in writing at your local store, because benefits and exclusions can differ by city and season.
